messages.subject: correctly inferring causality
parts:
Hi all,

I aim to test the causal direction of the relationship between "thermal traits" (latent), "personality" (latent), "Growth rate, GR" (measured), and "Metabolic rate, MR" (measured).

Below my 2 models, accompanied by the scheme of their structure (and the formulation of regressions - all other parts, i.e. latent structure and covariances, are identical).

Model #1 is for testing whether personality drives growth rate via affecting thermal traits and metabolic rate; the latter two traits are intrinsically correlated.


Model #2 is for testing whether thermal traits (and the correlated metabolic rate) drives growth rate through personality.



I had the impression that these 2 models would inform on the causality between the traits, yet both models have identical fitMeasures.

Have I been thinking about this in the wrong way? Could you suggest a better (or correct) way of testing my question?

Thanks a bunch already for any input.

Cheers
Ned

messages.author: 5abdb409f213d464
messages.subject: Re:  correctly inferring causality
parts:
I don't think you can test the causal direction without an experiment. You have to deduce this from theory or logically conclude and justify it. You could also test Thermal Traits -> Personality vs. Personality -> Thermal Traits. The fit would not change. The number of connections between the variables remains the same ...
